chapter: Properties of matter: elasticity, viscosity, surface tension

variants.title: Uniform bending: Young's modulus of a steel beam
variants.method: Uniform bending, equal loads beyond both knife edges
variants.note: Steel is the stiffest of these bars: the same load raises the middle least.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (Young's modulus of steel about 200 GPa)

variants.title: Uniform bending: Young's modulus of a brass beam
variants.method: Uniform bending, equal loads beyond both knife edges
variants.note: Brass is about half as stiff as steel, so the same load gives about twice the rise.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (Young's modulus of brass about 100 GPa)

variants.title: Uniform bending: Young's modulus of a copper beam
variants.method: Uniform bending, equal loads beyond both knife edges
variants.note: Copper is a little stiffer than brass; keep the load small so it stays elastic.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (Young's modulus of copper about 110 GPa)

variants.title: Uniform bending: Young's modulus of an aluminium beam
variants.method: Uniform bending, equal loads beyond both knife edges
variants.note: The most flexible bar of the set: the rise of the middle is large and easy to read.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (Young's modulus of aluminium about 69 GPa)
